 CENTER FOR RELIGION, CULTURE & DEMOCRACY
 D.C. FELLOWSHIP
 FOR CIVIC RENEWAL
JANUARY 2–6, 2027
 Forming faithful leaders to meet the political challenges of today and tomorrow 
 The D.C. Fellowship for Civic Renewal gives high-achieving students a fully funded opportunity to spend five days in the nation’s capital engaging in critical conversations with civic leaders. 
 WHAT IS THE
 D.C. Fellowship
 The D.C. Fellowship for Civic Renewal is a competitive program for about a dozen high-achieving students pursuing careers in law, public service, policy research, or related fields.  
 The Fellowship consists of lively discussions pertaining to our most pressing challenges in modern governance, such as political division, post-liberalism, the rise in antisemitism, attacks on the free market, religious institutions, and families. Discussions are led by prominent scholars, lawyers, and members of the federal judiciary.
 Outside of these sessions, students cultivate relationships with First Liberty staff and alumni of CRCD’s programs during meals and networking opportunities. Guided tours of venues such as the United States Capitol, the Supreme Court, and the U.S. Court of Federal Claims enrich themes and ideals discussed during the program. For over a decade, the D.C. Fellowship has called emerging leaders to engage modern-day challenges with conviction and prudence. Alumni of the D.C. Fellowship have answered that call—as clerks at the United States Court of Appeals, civil servants in the Department of Education and Department of Agriculture, staffers for members of Congress, and employees at leading think tanks.

 Who Should Apply?
 The D.C. Fellowship is ideal for high-achieving undergraduate students who aspire to careers in law, public service, policy, or related fields. Our fellows often come from programs in law, history, philosophy, and political science, but students from all disciplines of study are welcome.
 The dates for the D.C. Fellowship are January 2, 2027 – January 6, 2027.  
   The 2027 D.C. Fellowship applications are open now. Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis. The deadline to apply is November 13, 2026.

 Ready to Apply?
 Required application items include:  
 Completed online application
 Résumé
 Cover Letter
 Letter of Recommendation
 Writing Sample 
 Cover letters and writing samples must be original works not prepared using generative artificial intelligence. For questions regarding the application process, contact Jillian Barr at  jbarr@firstliberty.org . 
 Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis until November 13, 2026.
